findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - unwrap on fallible I/O operation
findings.failure_mode: Any file-not-found, permission, or I/O error aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and use .map_err(|e| Error::Io(e)) or equivalent typed error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() - unwrap on parse of untrusted input
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data (non-numeric value) panics the caller instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| Error::Parse) or similar typed error, then convert with u16::try_from

findings.problem: as u16 lossy width cast after parse
findings.failure_mode: Values in range 65536..u32::MAX silently truncate to u16, producing incorrect domain data without any error
findings.fix: Replace with u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| Error::Parse)?).map_err(|_| Error::Overflow) or parse directly to u16 with checked conversion

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields triggers panic via index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(Error::Invalid) to get name and value_str, then validate value_str is present

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: Same as above - a line missing the second field panics at index access

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) - hidden I/O side effect inside a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: Side effects leak into a function that should be data transformation; makes testing non-deterministic and couples parsing to console logging
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing logic. If logging is required, push it to the imperative shell caller that invokes load_frames

findings.problem: load_frames mixes file I/O, console logging, parsing, and collection in a single function
findings.failure_mode: Violates functional core / imperative shell: no pure layer is separable; cannot unit-test parsing logic in isolation without real files and console capture
findings.fix: Split into: (1) shell fn load_frames(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, E> that reads file and calls core, (2) pure fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, E> that handles parsing, (3) Record type with private fields and smart constructor

findings.problem: Record struct has public mutable fields (pub name: String, pub value: u16)
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct Record with empty name, invalid value range, or inconsistent state directly without any validation
findings.fix: Make fields private, add a fallible constructor fn new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Self, Error> that validates invariants, or use a newtype for name

findings.problem: println! inside an iterator map closure - side effect during collection
findings.failure_mode: Side effect order is tied to iterator evaluation order which is unspecified for parallel iterators; logging output is non-deterministic
findings.fix: Remove logging from the closure entirely; log in the shell layer after records are collected if needed

findings.problem: No try_reserve or capacity hint before Vec::collect on split output
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded reallocations on large files; OOM not handled gracefully - falls back to panic
findings.fix: Estimate line count or use try_reserve before the collect; count lines first or use a bounded parser

findings.problem: Collecting all split parts into Vec<String> when only 2 fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line; each line creates a Vec of Strings then clones into Record
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(Error::Invalid)? to get (name_str, value_str) without intermediate Vec, then parse value_str directly

findings.problem: load_frames returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper - all errors must panic
findings.failure_mode: Every failure mode (I/O, parse, invalid format, overflow) collapses into panic; callers cannot recover or distinguish error types
findings.fix: Define a typed enum Error { Io(io::Error), Parse, Invalid, Overflow } and return Result<Vec<Record>, Error>

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for this crate
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify performance claims or allocation behavior for file loading at scale
findings.fix: Add a benchmark measuring throughput vs file size, with allocation tracking (e.g., criterion with measurement of bytesallocated/op)

findings.problem: No cargo test, cargo fmt, or cargo clippy evidence provided
findings.failure_mode: Static review only; compilation, formatting, and lint compliance not verified
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, and cargo test to produce command evidence

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for file-loading throughput
no profiler data for allocation hotspots in load_frames
no allocation audit (try_reserve, Vec capacity) evidence
no behavior tests exercising invalid CSV lines, missing fields, or overflow values
no command evidence: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo test not run
residual_risk: Multiple BLOCKER findings: unwrap on I/O and parse, lossy as cast, unchecked indexing, hidden println! side effect, mixed imperative/pure responsibilities, no error taxonomy, and public mutable struct fields. The crate cannot be safely used without panicking on any malformed input or I/O error. All unwrap calls, the lossy cast, and unchecked indexing must be replaced with typed error handling before this code is safe for any production use. The functional core / imperative shell violation means parsing logic cannot be tested in isolation.
